rules.coverage_note: Which files are Vapor server files and which part of the server stack each one pulls in -- the router, Fluent and its driver (so: which database), Leaf, JWT, Queues. The module name is the import's own name, so no Pack field is needed, and the driver import is the only statement of the database an overlay can reach.

Which types register routes. A RouteCollection is the unit a Vapor project groups its endpoints into; the conformance is stated by relation.implements and the type is the declaration whose span contains it. The type is minted once, under the neutral hub key vapor:type:{path}:{type} as a VaporType with the same two attributes every rule gives it, and the classification lives in its own key space vapor:controller:{path}:{type} -- so a type that is both a Model and a Content payload keeps both entities and both conformance names instead of the alphabetically-first rule's kind winning the hub key (brief 3g, remedy 2).

Which types are Fluent models -- the types that back database tables. Six model protocols collapse into one rule over the conformance name. The type is minted once, under the neutral hub key vapor:type:{path}:{type} as a VaporType with the same two attributes every rule gives it, and the classification lives in its own key space vapor:model:{path}:{type} -- so a type that is both a Model and a Content payload keeps both entities and both conformance names instead of the alphabetically-first rule's kind winning the hub key (brief 3g, remedy 2).

Which types change the database schema. Both spellings of the protocol, sync and async, are one rule. The type is minted once, under the neutral hub key vapor:type:{path}:{type} as a VaporType with the same two attributes every rule gives it, and the classification lives in its own key space vapor:migration:{path}:{type} -- so a type that is both a Model and a Content payload keeps both entities and both conformance names instead of the alphabetically-first rule's kind winning the hub key (brief 3g, remedy 2).

What sits in front of a handler: middleware, authenticators and lifecycle handlers. Thirteen protocol spellings of one role become one rule. The type is minted once, under the neutral hub key vapor:type:{path}:{type} as a VaporType with the same two attributes every rule gives it, and the classification lives in its own key space vapor:middleware:{path}:{type} -- so a type that is both a Model and a Content payload keeps both entities and both conformance names instead of the alphabetically-first rule's kind winning the hub key (brief 3g, remedy 2).

Which types cross the wire -- the request and response bodies of this API. Content is Vapor's Codable-over-HTTP conformance and Validatable says the payload is checked on the way in. The type is minted once, under the neutral hub key vapor:type:{path}:{type} as a VaporType with the same two attributes every rule gives it, and the classification lives in its own key space vapor:payload:{path}:{type} -- so a type that is both a Model and a Content payload keeps both entities and both conformance names instead of the alphabetically-first rule's kind winning the hub key (brief 3g, remedy 2).

What runs outside a request: queued jobs, scheduled jobs and CLI commands. Six protocol spellings, one rule. The type is minted once, under the neutral hub key vapor:type:{path}:{type} as a VaporType with the same two attributes every rule gives it, and the classification lives in its own key space vapor:worker:{path}:{type} -- so a type that is both a Model and a Content payload keeps both entities and both conformance names instead of the alphabetically-first rule's kind winning the hub key (brief 3g, remedy 2).

Which URL a route serves, and which HTTP method answers it. omega-swift emits call.arguments on the same span as the call, carrying call.arg0_text -- the first argument with its quote bytes stripped -- so a Vapor route is keyed by what it serves, http:{method}:{normalized_route}, the identity every HTTP framework here mints. The method is the callee's own name, so eleven per-verb rules stay collapsed into one; requiring call.arg0 to begin with a quote keeps the rule to routes written with a literal path and drops dictionary.get(key) and the label-only spelling todos.get(use: index). The declaring function is the declaration whose span contains the call, which also covers a route written inside a group closure.

Which URLs a controller serves. The same match as vapor.route.registration plus the enclosing type, and it mints the Route under the identical key with the identical kind and the identical attributes, so the two rules agree on the identity (brief 3g) and the serves edge never dangles. It mints the neutral hub as well, because a type need not conform to RouteCollection to register a route.

Which path prefix the routes declared in this function sit under: routes.grouped("api", "v2"). The prefix is the first argument of the grouping call, reachable since omega-swift began emitting call.arguments, and it is route-normalized so a parameterised prefix agrees with the route spellings of every other framework. Only the first prefix component is stated -- grouped("api", "v2") gives /api -- and a group nested in another group is not folded in.

Which functions answer a request. A Vapor handler is recognised by taking a Request (or a WebSocket), a written type reaches the overlay as reference.type, so the handler is the function whose span contains that type mention and the controller is the type whose span contains the function.

Which columns back a Fluent model, and which of them are associations rather than scalars: @Parent, @Children and @Siblings carry the model graph. A Fluent property wrapper is written as a type identifier inside the property declaration, so fifteen wrapper spellings become one rule over the mention's own name, with the property and its model reached by span.

Which controllers, middleware, migrations and jobs this app actually installs: app.register(collection: TodoController()), app.middleware.use(APIKeyMiddleware()), app.migrations.add(CreateTodo()), routes.grouped(UserAuthenticator()). The component is a type constructed inside the installing call, which the Pack states as a call.swift whose span lies strictly inside it; the twenty-six lowercase-initial exclusions keep type constructors and drop ordinary calls. The target is the shared VaporTypeName node the declaration rules link to the declaring type, so this edge resolves across files -- the one cross-file answer Swift's names permit.

`todos.get(use: index)` and `todos.on(.PATCH, ":todoID", use: update)` register a route whose path is not the first argument -- it is inherited from the group, or it comes after the method. The registration is real and is stated where it is written; only its URL is not derivable here.

gaps: a route's URL is the first argument of the registration call only: todos.get("todos", ":id") states /todos, and the remaining path components are further arguments, for which the Pack publishes call.arg1 and call.arg2 with their quote bytes still on and no text form an identity could key on
routes.on(.PATCH, ":id", use: update) is not keyed by URL: its first argument is the method and the path is call.arg1, which carries its quotes
a group prefix is stated but not composed: a route inside routes.grouped("api") is keyed by its own path, not by /api joined to its path, because the overlay cannot concatenate two facts

a schema name (static let schema = "todos") and a @Field(key:) column name are string literals in a property initialiser and a property-wrapper attribute, neither of which is a call omega-swift emits call.arguments for
a route registered against a named handler (use: create) is not tied to that handler: call.last_arg for that spelling is the whole labelled argument, "use: create", not the function name
omega-swift publishes no receiver, so a route rule cannot separate app.get from dictionary.get and stays confidence: candidate
middleware ordering, dependency injection through Application storage and runtime router mutation are runtime semantics
